## Overview

Today you will be working with human population genomics data from the [1000 genomes project](https://www.internationalgenome.org/). The goal of this exercise is to provide real world experience using bioinformatics to examine genetic differences within and between populations. 

First, you will be assigned one of five regions (~2-10 Mb each) that I have targeted due to known signatures of importance in human evolution. Then, in Part 1, you will explore between population divergence specific to your region. The examination of these plots and statistics will be important in selecting populations to examine further for within population diversity and selection as part of Part 2. Finally, in Part 3, you will explore your region on the UCSC genome browser to examine potential genes that may contribute to the population genetic signal you see in your plots.

---

This exercise should provide a sense of how sliding window approaches are used to identify regions of interest in population genetics studies. Typically, these scans are done genome-wide along with other statistics to identify regions of interest. Then, gene annotations are used to find overlapping functional regions that can explain the genetic patterns. This can be done programmatically by downloading annotations from UCSC and using `bedtools` to intersect with the regions of interest. Then, [custom tracks](https://genome.ucsc.edu/goldenPath/help/customTrack.html) can be used to upload FST, pi, and Tajima's D results to the genome browser. We will discuss sliding window analyses in more depth in two weeks.
